public_rationale: The conditional forecast cannot yet be scored because its antecedent is unverified. The records establish an infrastructure commitment, active development and model training at Stargate. They do not establish the specified $100 billion versus $1 billion comparison or the resulting investment returns. No decisive event was located by October 28, 2026. Under the conditional-forecast rule, an unknown antecedent makes this not adjudicable at this freeze; it does not make Marcus right or wrong.
limitations: The evidence search cannot prove that no qualifying investment exists.
Later Stargate announcements cannot automatically be treated as the same investment described in March 2024.
Company-wide losses, revenue growth and financing would not by themselves settle project economics.

statement.excerpt: Even if a $100B LLM worked noticeably better than a $1B LLM, the economics for that investment are problematic.
statement.document_title: The Second Worst $100B Investment in The History of AI?

from_speaker: worked noticeably better than a $1B LLM
the economics for that investment are problematic
customers probably would not be willing to pay the required premium
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading of problematic economics is difficulty recovering the investment and operating costs from customer payments while earning a commercial return.
The $100 billion refers to the model and its supporting infrastructure, consistent with the surrounding passage. It is not necessarily the cost of one training run.
The condition requires a roughly $100 billion investment producing a model demonstrably better than a roughly $1 billion alternative, with both costs measured comparably.
The surrounding 2028–2030 dates describe planned deployment, not a deadline for investment recovery. The economic forecast has no stated deadline.
The investment amount has an estimate basis because the context attributes it to press reporting.
criteria.support_condition: After the performance and investment condition is established, attributable costs, customer payments and returns show that the investment cannot reasonably recover its capital and operating costs with a commercial return over its economic life.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After the same condition is established, attributable customer cash flows demonstrate recovery of the investment and operating costs with a commercial return.
